pairs.question: Cicero meus quid aget?
pairs.answer: Iste vero sit in sinu semper et complexu meo.
pairs.derivation: Self-posed-and-answered. Source: 'Quid? Cicero meus quid aget? iste vero sit in sinu semper et complexu meo.' Dropped the leading framing exclamation 'Quid?'; kept the operative interrogative 'Cicero meus quid aget?'. The reply directly answers it (what my Cicero will do: be ever in my embrace). Answer is the contiguous first sentence; capitalized 'iste'->'Iste' as presentation normalization. The neighboring questions in this letter (Rogem te ut venias? / Non rogem? / Sine te igitur sim?; quid Tulliola mea fiet?) were dropped: their follow-ups are anguished fragments or explicit deferrals ('iam id vos videte: mihi deest consilium') that do not actually answer.
